texts.label: A
fehler: "The chapel was empty at four a.m." – a few lines later a man is sitting there; this is a logic break.
"It wasn't a question." – a stock cliché, which the brief explicitly rules out.
"The silence felt different now, thinner." – this tells the reader instead of showing.
"It was just a plastic rectangle with a photo and a title." – a badge with no name is barely plausible, and the sentence is laboured.
At roughly 180 words the text falls well short of the requested 250; the stain image at the end feels heavy with symbolism.

texts.label: B
fehler: "She stood and smoothed the front of her trousers." – a slightly stock gesture.
"Neither of them looked at the cup." – a touch over-pointed and deliberate.
"He had placed both shoes squarely beneath his knees." – a slightly awkward image: the feet are in the shoes.

texts.label: C
fehler: "the third-floor air tasted like copper and bleach" – a well-worn hospital cliché.
"Hospital policy dictated she ask" – explanatory and bureaucratic telling.
"She mentally ran through the charts" – an explaining interior report.
"He couldn't have read it." – spells out the mystery for the reader.
At about 300 words the text runs clearly over length; the bruise and the shift-swap knowledge overload the scene with clues.

texts.label: D
fehler: "She had seen people sit like that a thousand times." – a cliché.
"She had not told him her name. She had not said anything at all." – redundant underlining of the point.
"Not yet, maybe." / "I wanted to see the room first." – edges close to an ominous revelation.
"A crow lifted off the top level" – the closing image is somewhat generic and switches location.
At about 310 words the text is over length.

texts.label: E
fehler: "she heard herself ask" – a stock phrase.
"He shook his head, not unkindly." – a well-worn formula.
"watched it as though it were a fire" – the closing comparison is slightly too knowing.
"as if he'd been handed something and then asked to give it back" – an overwrought simile.
